title: Practice Objectivity
coreMove: Strip fear, ego, and wishful story away from the facts before deciding what kind of obstacle you are facing.
sourcePressure: This chapter belongs to Perception, so it must teach cleaner seeing before it teaches action or endurance. Source sidecar ch04 exists and provides partial-source support only; no full text is frozen. For "Practice Objectivity", the pressure is to teach this exact move: Strip fear, ego, and wishful story away from the facts before deciding what kind of obstacle you are facing.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version turns the chapter into generic mindset advice instead of a precise discipline of reading the obstacle cleanly. For "Practice Objectivity", avoid replacing the chapter move with the whole book thesis.

sourceAnchors.name: John D. Rockefeller
sourceAnchors.detail: Frozen notes link Rockefeller to objectivity under pressure in the Perception section.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Rockefeller can appear as an image of refusing to price events through panic before reading the actual facts.

hook: A generic obstacle appears and teaches practice objectivity
The problem is not the problem
Everything changed when the setback arrived
counterintuition: The obstacle is actually a blessing
The hard part is really your mindset
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on adversity
Write down three things you are grateful for
Take a breath and choose courage

exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
